subject: VPC commercial: fixed-node vs consumption anchoring
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@healthtech.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthtech.com
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: VPC commercial: fixed-node vs consumption anchoring

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — HealthTech Labs is interested in moving a pilot to private VPC. Before we lock a time with procurement/legal, procurement asked for a clear pricing comparison:

- A fixed-node (site) license quote for a 3-node pilot and what scaling to 10 nodes would look like
- A consumption/usage-based alternative (billing per vGPU-hour or equivalent) with expected unit economics for our workload (documented assumptions appreciated)
- How the platform fee is applied between hosted vs private: is it a flat fee, per-node, or amortized?
- Support tiers (SLA, on-call, response windows) and rough costs for each

Compliance note: pilot must be EU data residency, SOC2 is mandatory, and we need audit log export sample.

Can you send a short side-by-side and any attachments you typically share for procurement review? Procurement timeline is tight — aiming to review commercials this week.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of IT Procurement
HealthTech Labs
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@healthtech.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthtech.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-01T12:30:00+00:00
Subject: Re: VPC commercial: fixed-node vs consumption anchoring

Hi Liam — thanks, and great to hear HealthTech is ready to pilot. High-level comparison below (I kept it compact for procurement). I'll attach our pricing workbook and a starter SOW in a follow-up from Marissa.

Option A — Fixed (site) license
- 3-node pilot: flat annual license for nodes + one-time onboarding. Pricing examples: €85k–€110k/year for pilot (includes platform fee + operator licenses), scales to predictable per-node pricing for 10-node.
- Platform fee is charged as a fixed annual item for private deployments; operator licenses are per-seat if the customer chooses to manage operator access.

Option B — Consumption (metered)
- Billed on vGPU-hours with a minimum monthly floor. Better if workload is spiky. Example: €X per vGPU-hour (we'll provide estimate numbers once we have expected qps/peak sequences).
- Platform fee applied as a smaller base month-to-month charge; unit price per vGPU-hour is higher than amortized fixed-node when utilization is steady.

Option C — Hybrid (anchored commitment + overage)
- Commitment to a baseline (e.g., capacity equivalent to 5 nodes) with a reduced platform fee amortized across committed capacity, overage billed consumption-style. Good middle ground for predictable cost with burst flexibility.

Support tiers (examples)
- Standard: business-hours email support, SLA on Sev1 8 business hours, includes ticketing and monthly health check.
- Premium: 24x7 SRE on-call escalation, Sev1 2 hours (response/ack), two on-site or remote onboarding days.
- Enterprise: Dedicated SRE war room, guaranteed incident bridge within 1 hour, quarterly architecture reviews, optional retained engineering hours.

Quick asks from our side so we can firm up numbers:
1) Pilot size in terms of expected concurrent requests (qps) and typical sequence length
2) Whether you prefer a fully-managed operator model or customer-managed operator licenses
3) Any required retention windows for logs/audit samples

I'll tee up a short pricing workbook and draft SOW after Monica and Marissa confirm the commercial levers. Would a 30–45m call tomorrow at 14:00 CET work to walk procurement through this?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@healthtech.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthtech.com, Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthtech.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T15:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: VPC commercial: fixed-node vs consumption anchoring

Karthik — thanks for the breakdown. A few clarifications to help your estimators:

- Pilot intent: steady baseline processing for nightly batch indexing and 6–8 concurrent interactive sessions during business hours. Estimate ~4 vGPUs in steady state, spikes to ~8 for short windows.
- We will manage operator access internally (so operator licenses would be customer-managed seats).
- Retention: audit logs for 12 months, and ability to export logs in CSV/JSON on request for audits.
- SOC2: we need the SOC2 report and a short note on how audit logs can be exported/streamed to our SIEM.

We prefer predictable budgeting but are open to hybrid if the amortized platform fee is capped for the first 12 months (procurement wants to avoid surprise platform fee increases during pilot).

Yes, tomorrow 14:00 CET works — locking it in. Also attaching our procurement checklist (see attachment).

Cheers,
Liam
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@healthtech.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-02T08:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: VPC commercial: fixed-node vs consumption anchoring

Hi Liam — looping in the proposed commercial artifacts. Attached: Redwood_Proposed_Pricing_v3.xlsx and a draft SOW (SOW_HealthTech_v1.docx). Key points we put into the workbook given your inputs:

- Pilot pricing: line-itemed as (A) Pilot fixed-node 3-node annual license = €95,000 (platform fee included) + onboarding €12,000; (B) Consumption estimate: floor 150 vGPU-hours/month at €Y per hour with an estimated monthly run-rate of ~€12k based on your steady-state assumptions.
- Hybrid option: we propose anchoring at 5-node equivalent for the first 12 months and capping platform fee increase to 0% during pilot. Overage priced at consumption rates.
- Support: we list Standard / Premium / Enterprise with concrete response SLAs and optional retained engineering blocks. For pilot we recommend Premium for the first 90 days (one week of on-call onboarding days included at no additional charge).
- Discounting: for a 3-year committed conversion after pilot we are recommending a 15% platform-fee discount and a one-time migration credit of €50,000 to HealthTech Labs. For 12–24 month commitments, discount tiers are 7.5%–12%.

Compliance: SOC2 report and an audit-logs export runbook are included in the attachments (HealthTech_Procurement_Checklist.pdf includes the specific data points you requested). If legal needs the SOC2 artifact or attestations, we can queue that with security; I copied Monica for the SSO/KMS/Kubernetes control-plane questions.

Can we ask procurement for a single-sheet signoff that lists their preferred path (Fixed / Consumption / Hybrid) so we can fast-track legal redlines?

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_Pricing_v3.xlsx, SOW_HealthTech_v1.docx (draft), HealthTech_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference
